tagline: Off the interstate and down to the falcons' canyon.
intro: From exit 44 at Meridian, Idaho 69 runs south eight miles to Kuna, which began as a railroad stop with a coach on to Boise. There the byway, once a route for miners and homesteaders, turns down Swan Falls Road through farmland and then rocky country into the Morley Nelson Snake River Birds of Prey National Conservation Area. It comes to the Snake River at Swan Falls Dam and turns west toward Celebration Park.
More than 700 pairs of raptors, of 15 species, nest on the canyon walls. Out on the plateau, by the Bureau of Land Management's count, live the densest ground squirrel populations ever recorded.

moments.title: Kuna
moments.text: The town likes to say its name means the end of the trail, though one early account has it as a Shoshone word for green leaf, good to smoke.

moments.title: Swan Falls Dam
moments.text: The oldest hydroelectric dam on the Snake, built in 1901 where the Bonneville Flood once came through at 33 million cubic feet a second.

moments.title: Celebration Park
moments.text: Petroglyphs here go back more than 12,000 years, and the 1897 Guffey railroad bridge, built to haul Silver City ore to Nampa, now carries walkers and riders over the Snake.
